ECE 6390 / Waves and fields

Standing waves

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how reflection superposes traveling waves into a pattern with stationary nodes.

A forward wave and a reflected wave propagate in opposite directions. Their relative phase varies with position, creating an amplitude envelope even though both constituent waves travel.

For incident amplitude 1 and reflected amplitude |Γ|, the envelope extremes are 1 + |Γ| and 1 − |Γ| in a lossless passive-reflection example. Exact nodes require equal amplitudes.

Adjacent envelope minima are separated by λ/2. The standing-wave ratio is (1 + |Γ|)/(1 − |Γ|) for |Γ| below 1; phase shifts move the envelope along the axis.

Example

With |Γ| = 0.5, the envelope ranges from 0.5 to 1.5, giving a standing-wave ratio of 3. The minima remain above zero.

    Practice

    1. A reflected field has one quarter the incident amplitude. Find the envelope minimum, maximum, and standing-wave ratio.

    Use field amplitudes 1 − |Γ| and 1 + |Γ|.

    The minimum is 0.75, the maximum is 1.25, and their ratio is 5/3 ≈ 1.667.
